text.p: - Slovenia's Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler visits his Russian counterpart Yevgeny Primakov in Moscow on Friday, where they will discuss bilateral cooperation and NATO enlargement.

- The government said it will propose changes to the law to prevent foreign owners getting back their forestry estates that were nationalised after World War Two. The return of land to the church remains to be discussed.

- Slovenia's March credit rating remained unchanged at DB3a, credit rating agency Dun & Bradstreet said. The agency placed Slovenia second in the region, just behind the Czech Republic and ahead of Poland.

- Slovenian president Milan Kucan met the new cabinet on Thursday and congratulated the ruling coalition parties, centre-left Liberal Democrats and conservative People's Party for their cooperation in the interest of the country.
- Ljubljana University students threatened to organize protests in April against the government's decision to hike car insurance prices by 35 percent for people under 25 years old.

- In 1996, the government issued 70 state guarantees for loans to Slovenian companies to a total value of 71.5 billion tolars ($455.4 million). Most of the funding went to the nuclear power plant in Krsko and the state's motorway company. The government plans to spend around the same amount this year.
- In the last few years, the number of employees in the textile industry fell by about 25 percent following a global decline in the sector, the Economic Activities Ministry said.
- Slovenia's Andreja Grasic on Thursday won first place in the biathlon World Cup race of 15 km (nine miles) in Nagano.
- Listed food producer Droga Portoroz said on Thursday its unrevised 1996 net profit rose 30 percent to 800 million tolars as a result of an increase in sales and cost-cutting measures..
- Slovenia's Smelt Olimpija lost a Euroleague basketball match against Croatian Ciobona in Zagreb on Thursday by 61-58.
- Slovenian authorities on Thursday arrested an Austrian citizen who tried to smuggle a large amount of infantry weapons over the border.
- Listed construction firm GPG said its unrevised 1996 pre-tax profit was expected to rise to 109.5 million tolars from 12 million in 1995.

- Slovenia's 1996 trade deficit fell to $853 million, down from $953.5 million in 1995, the Bank of Slovenia said. The current account was again positive at $46.4 million, up from a deficit of $36 million the previous year, the bank said.
